clue.text: Wasp I distracted circling plant

indicators.note: the words 'Wasp I distracted' surround the answer, so it sits inside them, read straight through

explanation.surface: A wasp buzzing round a houseplant has the speaker distracted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' looks like what the wasp does, but it says the letters run inside wASP I DISTRActed.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy leafy houseplant, famously the Victorian parlour favourite.

clue.text: They progress in leaps and bounds before eating cane up

definitions.text: They progress in leaps and bounds

indicators.note: one word eating another takes it inside, so the word for before swallows the next piece

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, familiar from 'ante-room'

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' says the word for cane is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a cane is a long stick or pole

explanation.surface: Someone advances fast before snacking on a stick of cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They' fits a singular-looking answer because antelope is its own plural; 'up' works as a reversal only because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are swift grazing animals that run with great springing strides across the plains.

clue.text: Small miner strips vertical end of quarry

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for strips is entered going upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to strip something, such as bark or paint, is to peel it, so strips gives peels

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of 'quarry'

explanation.surface: A little miner strips a sheer rock face at the far end of the quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vertical' turns PEELS into SLEEP, then Y ends 'quarry'. The miner is one of the seven dwarfs from Snow White, who dig in a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy is one of Disney's seven dwarfs, who work all day in a diamond mine.

clue.text: Grasp front of tartan rug

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, taken from 'tartan'

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig or toupee

explanation.surface: Someone seizes the leading edge of a tartan rug.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is an informal British verb for understanding something suddenly, to grasp it.

clue.text: What ass does to curb lazy women's rides

indicators.note: to curb is to hem in, so the donkey's noise encloses the lazy women

parts.note: a donkey brays
lazy means idle
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A donkey stubbornly restrains idle women on their pony rides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to curb' puts IDLEW inside BRAYS. 'curb' and 'rides' tempt you to think of bridles, which is part of the answer by coincidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride is a track for horse riding, which is exactly what a bridleway is in Britain.

clue.text: How to shelter border road initially? This'll do it

definitions.text: How to shelter border road initially? This'll do it

indicators.note: to shelter something is to surround and protect it, so the word how encloses the next pieces

parts.note: a border is an edge

indicators.note: the first letter, here of 'road'

explanation.surface: A question about protecting the edge of a road, answered by the very thing that does it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a hedgerow is just what shelters a road's border, so the final question is answered by the wordplay itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedgerow is a row of bushes along a field or lane, giving shelter from wind.

clue.text: Clasp ring found in ancient tower

indicators.note: the ring is found inside the tower, so its letter goes within

parts.note: a broch is an Iron Age round stone tower found in Scotland
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An old ring with a clasp is unearthed in an ancient tower.
explanation.walkthrough: BROCH, a prehistoric drystone tower of northern Scotland, may be unfamiliar.
explanation.definitionFit: A brooch is an ornament fastened to clothing with a pin and clasp.

clue.text: Union probing phone system's boss

indicators.note: a probe goes into something, so the union's letter goes inside

parts.note: STD is subscriber trunk dialling, the old British direct-dial system

explanation.surface: A trade union investigates who runs the telephone company.
explanation.walkthrough: STD, the old British subscriber trunk dialling code system, may be unknown outside the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised knob or stud, as on a shield or a leather belt.

clue.text: Wildfowlers besiege a French plant

indicators.note: to besiege is to surround, so the jumbled letters enclose the French word
wild describes something unruly, so the letters of fowlers run riot

parts.note: taken as written
un is French for a

explanation.surface: Duck hunters surround a French factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wildfowlers' must be split: 'Wild' makes SFLOWER of 'fowlers', which goes round UN.
explanation.definitionFit: The sunflower is a tall plant grown for its huge yellow flower heads and oily seeds.

clue.text: Heron, say, on top of tree

parts.note: EG, for example, is what 'say' means when introducing an instance
re means on, concerning

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter, from 'tree'

explanation.surface: A heron, for instance, perches at the top of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heron, say' looks like the definition by example; 'say' actually gives EG.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white member of the heron family of wading birds.

clue.text: One cold diver turns over chunk of glacier

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: turning over makes the word for the bird read backwards

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A shivering diver flips over beside a lump of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diver' is a bird, not a swimmer; GREBE becomes EBERG.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceberg is a large mass of ice that has broken from a glacier into the sea.

clue.text: Feature in garden party with superb sandwiches

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: to sandwich is to enclose between, so the word for superb holds the short form of with

parts.note: superb, informally, means very good

explanation.surface: A garden party where splendid sandwiches are the highlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food at the party, but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogwood is a flowering shrub often planted as an ornamental garden feature.

clue.text: Whitish yellow growth that climbs walls

indicators.note: to wall is to enclose, so the plant surrounds the yellow

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A yellowish creeper that climbs up walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walls' reads as a noun the plant climbs, but it is the verb for enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is a creamy off-white colour, like elephant tusk, so a pale yellowish white.

clue.text: Plant English or Greek character in plot

indicators.note: these pieces sit inside the word for plot

parts.note: a garden plot is a bed
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Choosing whether an English or Greek figure goes into a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a storyline, but it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The bee orchid is a European wild orchid whose flower mimics a female bee.

clue.text: Fly low with daring

parts.note: to feel low is to feel blue
bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: Flying low takes some nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTLE as nerve is British slang, as in 'lose your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebottle is a large buzzing blowfly with a metallic blue body.

clue.text: Vet books inspired by excited toddler

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the jumbled letters take in the books
an excited child is agitated and jumbled, so the letters of toddler are rearranged

parts.note: lit is short for literature, books

explanation.surface: An animal doctor's reading list was prompted by an enthusiastic little child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges TODDLER into DRDOTLE, which 'inspired by' fills with LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Dolittle is Hugh Lofting's fictional animal doctor who talks to his patients.

clue.text: TV documentary strand animating a rather dull town

indicators.note: animating means livening up and stirring, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A television nature series brings life to an otherwise boring town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Natural World is a long-running BBC series of wildlife documentary films.

clue.text: A Greek heretic dealing with land

parts.note: an Arian followed Arius, who denied Christ's full divinity

explanation.surface: A Greek dissenter who gets involved in land disputes.
explanation.walkthrough: ARIAN, a follower of the 4th-century heretic Arius, not ARYAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrarian describes things relating to farming and the cultivation of fields.

clue.text: Councillor's wearing jumper and vest for Swedes, maybe

parts.note: roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumping animal

indicators.note: the councillor wears the top, so its letters are inside the garment

parts.note: a vest is a sleeveless top

explanation.surface: A councillor dressed in a sweater and vest for a meeting with Scandinavians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' and 'vest' suggest clothes, but the jumper is a kangaroo. Swedes are swede turnips, not people; the plural stands for the crop as a class.
explanation.definitionFit: Swede, like turnip and carrot, is a vegetable grown for its edible root.

clue.text: A Dubliner's about to take in dress for tiny bodies

indicators.note: the reversed name takes the dress inside it
about means turned round, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish first name, so a Dubliner
a robe is a dress or gown

explanation.surface: An Irishman puts on a frock to look at microbes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the Irish name to NAES; Sean stands for any Dubliner, as Paddy or Mick might.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaerobes are microorganisms that live without oxygen, such as many bacteria.

clue.text: Nuts like tackling digital problem

indicators.note: tackling here means getting to grips with, the word for like grips the problem

parts.note: as means like
a corn is a painful hard patch on a toe, a digit

explanation.surface: Crazy people treating a computer glitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' suggests computing, but it means of the fingers and toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Acorns are the nuts of the oak tree.

clue.text: Briefly recognise lakes and hillock

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word for recognise loses its last letter

parts.note: to recognise someone is to know them
L is the abbreviation for lake, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A quick glimpse of lakes and a small hill in the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A knoll is a small rounded hill, the same as a hillock.

clue.text: Stimulate class left without paper

parts.note: a kind is a class or sort

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the word left loses the paper's letters

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Spur on a group that has been left with no newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle interest is to arouse or excite it, as a spark lights a fire.

clue.text: Problem in 8 for possibly blocking sound of 25?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters block the middle of the owl's call by sitting inside it

parts.note: the call of an owl, the 25 across answer, is a hoot

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of for could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An ailment at a stud farm that might be muffling an owl's call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges 'for' to OFR. Answer 8 is STUD, a horse-breeding farm, and 25 is the little owl, whose call is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoof rot is a bacterial infection of livestock feet, a disease that could affect a stud's horses.

clue.text: Ditch one hectare after another

indicators.note: after means one piece follows the other in the answer

parts.note: HA is the abbreviation for a hectare
another means one more hectare, so the abbreviation again

explanation.surface: A trench is dug one hectare at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch with a wall, bounding a park without blocking the view.

clue.text: Crew unknown yacht that's docked in Douglas?

parts.note: to crew a ship is to man it
X is the algebraic unknown
a cat, short for catamaran, is a type of yacht

explanation.surface: A mystery crew aboard a yacht moored in the Isle of Man's harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' suggests a moored boat, but means tail-less. Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx breed of cat from the Isle of Man is born with little or no tail.

clue.text: Flyer's second article abridged

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the article loses its final letter

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A pilot's next piece of writing has been cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: A moth is a winged insect, so something that flies.

clue.text: Hard woman rejected cosmetic

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the name reads backwards

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A harsh woman turned down the make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish plant dye used to colour hair and decorate skin.

clue.text: It flies Times into oil well at sea

indicators.note: the abbreviations go into the jumbled letters
at sea means confused, so the letters of oil well are mixed up

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so two of them stand for times

explanation.surface: A newspaper is dropped onto an offshore oil rig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is two T's, for time. 'at sea' rearranges OIL WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: The little owl is a small owl species of Europe, a bird that flies.
